> 信言不美，美言不信.

The last chapter closes the book in a particular way: it does not give an answer. It crosses out nine things.

Count the 不's: 不美, 不信, 不辯, 不善, 不博, 不知, 不積, 不害, 不爭. Nine.

The first eighty chapters hold 5,138 characters and 231 不's. This chapter puts nine of them into about sixty characters — the highest density in the book.

## Why close with nine negatives

Because at the end Laozi will not say "this is the way." He will only say: not this, not this, not this.

The first sentence of the book crosses out one — 道可道，非恒道.
The last sentence crosses out nine — 為而不爭.

The eighty chapters in between are about how what remains after the crossing-out manages to live.

## 信 is a person and a word

信: 人言為信 — a person's word.

The character is built from 人 and 言, and the definition is the construction: what a person says, standing behind it.

So 信言不美 is not "honest speech is plain." It is: the word that has a person behind it is not 美.

## 美 is "delicious"

美: 甘也, from 羊 and 大 — the big sheep, sweet to eat.

The book uses 美 eight times. Seven of those are accusations:

- 天下皆知美之為美，斯惡已 (ch2) — knowing beauty as beauty is already ugliness.
- 美言可以市尊 (ch62) — fine words traded for rank.
- 美之為美 (ch2 again in the same line's argument).

And one occurrence passes: 美其服 (ch80), where the subject is the person wearing the clothes.

This chapter is 美's last appearance, and it is its heaviest: 信言不美.

## 善者不辯

善 is not moral goodness here. 善 in the book mostly means skill — 善建者, 善戰者, 善攝生. The one who is good at a thing does not argue about it.

辯 is the split tongue: 言 with 辡, two sides facing each other. Argument is structurally paired, and the paired thing is what chapter 68 removed.

## 知者不博，博者不知

Knows and is not broad; broad and does not know.

博 is width — the accumulation of coverage. The chapter puts width on the same list as the other eight, which is the most uncomfortable line in it for anyone who reads for a living.

## 聖人不積

Does not store.

既以為人，己愈有；既以與人，己愈多 — the more he does for others, the more he has; the more he gives, the more he has.

The mechanism is the one from chapter 81's own first line: what is held is a claim, and a claim has to be defended. What has been given has no such edge.

## 天之道，利而不害；聖人之道，為而不爭

The way of heaven benefits and does not harm; the way of the sage acts and does not contend.

利 — the blade and the grain: to bring increase. 害 — to cut into.

Two verbs on the same material: 利 brings the harvest in, 害 cuts. The difference is not the amount of force but its direction.

And 為而不爭 — the last four characters of the book. Acting, and without a counterpart.

## The whole arc

Chapter 1 crossed out one word.
Chapter 81 crosses out nine.
Everything between is the practice of living in what is left.

That is the book's shape, and it is why the last chapter refuses to conclude: a conclusion would be the tenth 不 that turned into a 是.
